speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of talk about productivity gains through AI.
zh: 有很多关于通过 AI 提高生产力的讨论。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 有这么一类人，他们过度炒作，什么都没起作用，实际上没有人以规模采用这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see a significant amount of games.
zh: 我们看到大量的游戏。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们发现非常非常 AI 前卫的工程团队报告说每周节省大约 8 到 10 小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whenever I hear a stat like this, I think an important element is this is the worst it will ever be.
zh: 每当我听到这样的统计数据时，我认为一个重要的要素是这是它曾经最糟糕的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is now the baseline.
zh: 这现在是基准线。

speaker: Unknown
en: The truth is the value is changing every day, so you need to ride that wave along with it.
zh: 真相是价值每天都在变化，所以你需要随着它一起驾驭那个浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a story I heard you share on a different podcast where there's an engineer who has Goose watching.
zh: 我听到你在另一个播客上分享过一个故事，那里有一个工程师让 Goose 盯着。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll be talking to a colleague on Slack or an email, and they'll be discussing some feature that they think is useful to implement.
zh: 你会在 Slack 或邮件上与同事交谈，他们会讨论一些他们认为实现起来有用的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now a few hours later, he'll find that Goose has already tried to build that feature and opened a PR for it on Git.
zh: 现在几个小时后，他会发现 Goose 已经尝试构建那个功能并在 Git 上打开了一个 PR。

speaker: Unknown
en: What level of engineer is most benefiting from these tools?
zh: 什么级别的工程师最从这些工具中受益？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's been surprising and really amazing, the non-technical people using AI agents and programming tools to build things, the people that are able to embrace it to optimize for their particular workday and their particular set of tasks are really showing the most impact from these tools.
zh: 令人惊讶且真正惊人的一件事是，非技术人员使用 AI 智能体和编程工具来构建东西，那些能够拥抱它以针对他们特定的工作日和特定的一组任务进行优化的人，真正展示了来自这些工具的最多影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think things will look in a couple of years in terms of how engineers work that's different from today?
zh: 你认为几年后事情在工程师如何工作方面看起来会如何，这与今天不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: All these LLMs are sitting idle overnight and on weekends, while humans aren't there.
zh: 所有这些 LLM 晚上和周末闲置在那里，而人类不在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no need for that.
zh: 没有必要那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should be working all the time.
zh: 它们应该一直工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: They should be trying to build in anticipation of what we want.
zh: 它们应该尝试预先构建我们想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's maybe the most counterintuitive lesson you've learned about building products or building teams?
zh: 关于构建产品或构建团队，你学到的最反直觉的教训可能是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of engineers think that code quality is important to building a successful product.
zh: 许多工程师认为代码质量对于构建成功的产品很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The two have nothing to do with each other.
zh: 这两者彼此没有任何关系。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 在我们的对话中，我们聊到了他们内部的开源智能体叫 Goose，根据他们的衡量，这为员工平均每周节省 8 到 10 小时的工作时间，而且那个数字正在上升，AI 具体如何使他们的团队更有生产力以及最受益的团队。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 有趣的是，它不是工程团队，转变文化以变得非常 AI 导向需要什么，他们在内部做出的非常无聊的改变，这比任何 AI 工具更多地提高了生产力。

en: Make code back prototypes and apps fast with Figma Make.
zh: 使用 Figma Make 快速制作代码支撑的原型和应用程序。

en: Check it out at figma.com/lenny.

en: Dhanji, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Dhanji，非常感谢你的到来，欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you Lenny.
zh: 谢谢 Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great pleasure to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with a letter that I hear you wrote to Jack Dorsey to convince him that he and that Block needed to take AI a lot more seriously.
zh: 我想从听说你写给 Jack Dorsey 的一封信开始，你写这封信是为了说服他和 Block 需要认真对待 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you called it your AI manifesto and it seems like it really worked.
zh: 我想你称它为你的 AI 宣言，而且它似乎真的奏效了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to talk a lot about the changes that came as a result of that.
zh: 我们将大量谈论因此而产生的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me just ask, what did you say in this letter and what happened right after you sent that letter to him?
zh: 所以我就问问，你在信中说了什么，在你把信寄给他之后紧接着发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So about two and a half years ago or so, Jack really felt like things needed to change.
zh: 所以大约两年半前，Jack 真的觉得事情需要改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he had a sense that the industry was going in a different direction.
zh: 我觉得他感觉到行业正朝着不同的方向发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he got about 40 of the company's top executives into a room on a weekly basis, and they all used to sort of talk everything through that was going on and he added me to that group.
zh: 所以他每周把公司大约 40 名最高高管聚集到一个房间里，他们过去通常把发生的所有事情都从头到尾谈一遍，他把我加到了那个小组。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at some point, I observed that we were talking about lots of deep things, lots of relevant things, but no one was really paying attention to AI, and so that's when I wrote that letter.
zh: 所以在某个时刻，我观察到我们谈论很多深层次的事情，很多相关的事情，但没有人真正关注 AI，所以我写了那封信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be honest, it's I think taken on a life of its own, but there wasn't much to the letter other than I think we should do this.
zh: 老实说，我认为这封信已经自行发展了它的生命，但除了我认为我们应该做这件事之外，信里其实没什么别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we should do it centrally and it's important for us to be ahead of the game and be an AI native company because that's where the industry is heading.
zh: 我认为我们应该集中做这件事，这对我们要领先于游戏并成为一家 AI 原生公司很重要，因为那是行业发展的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me just say it's important to note you were not CTO at this point.
zh: 我只想说，值得注意的是，你当时不是 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were just a senior engineer kind of person?
zh: 你只是一名高级工程师类型的人？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, yeah, in fact, I was part-time at the time because I had just had a kid and I was coming back in and I was helping out one of the engineering teams and then Jack came over to Sydney and spent two days with me and both of us like long walks.
zh: 不，是的，实际上我当时是兼职，因为我刚有了孩子，我正在回来工作，我在帮助一个工程团队，然后 Jack 来到悉尼，和我待了两天，我们俩都进行了长距离散步。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we walked all around Sydney and talked it through up and down, and then yeah, he offered me the job and I thought it was a great opportunity once in a lifetime, so I took it.
zh: 所以我们绕着悉尼走了一圈，反复讨论了这件事，然后，是的，他给了我这份工作，我认为这是一个千载难逢的好机会，所以我接受了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like be careful what you're good at sort of situation.
zh: 这就像是“小心你擅长的事情”那种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what were some of the bigger changes that you made after Jack is on board and Block execs are on board of are, "Cool, this is completely right.
zh: 那么在 Jack 上船、Block 高管们也上船之后，你做的一些重大改变是什么，他们觉得，“酷，这完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to go much bigger and think much more deeply about how AI is changing, how we build and how we should build."
zh: 我们需要做得更大，并更深入地思考 AI 如何改变我们的构建方式以及我们应该如何构建。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Or some of the bigger changes that you made from a perspective of other companies listening to this, trying to think about what they should be doing?
zh: 或者对于正在收听这个节目的其他公司来说，他们试图思考自己应该做什么，你做的一些重大改变是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: At the start, my main focus was to get block to think like a technology company.
zh: 起初，我的主要重点是让 Block 像一家技术公司那样思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for a long time we had had a little bit of, I'm going to call it identity drift, maybe.
zh: 在很长一段时间里，我有一点，我要称之为身份漂移，也许吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were talking about ourselves as a financial services company.
zh: 我们把自己称为一家金融服务公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people called us FinTech, all of this stuff.
zh: 有些人称我们为 FinTech，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I started working at what was then known as Square, we were always thought of as a technology company just like Google or Facebook or any of the others.
zh: 但是当我在当时被称为 Square 的地方开始工作时，我们总是被认为是一家技术公司，就像 Google 或 Facebook 或其他任何公司一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I wanted to get us back to that.
zh: 所以我想让我们回到那个状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the first thing I did was to try and institute a number of programs that focused on that.
zh: 所以我做的第一件事是尝试设立许多专注于此的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everything from getting the top ICs in the company together to talk to each other, to starting a whole bunch of special projects.
zh: 所以从把公司的高级技术负责人聚集在一起互相交谈，到启动一系列特殊项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we got about two to five engineers per project.
zh: 所以每个项目我们大约有 2 到 5 名工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were about eight or nine different projects and we had reinstituted, the company-wide hack week.
zh: 大约有八九个不同的项目，我们恢复了全公司范围的黑客周。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all of this just kind of created a little bit of a spark of, "Hey, we're building technology again, we're trying to push the frontier again."
zh: 所以所有这些只是创造了一点火花，“嘿，我们又在构建技术了，我们又试图推动前沿了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how it started, and then there were a whole number of steps after that where we went from a GM structure to a functional org structure, which was I think the key to making our transformation into being more of an AI-native company.
zh: 事情就是这样开始的，然后在那之后有一系列步骤，我们从 GM 结构转变为职能型组织结构，我认为这是我们要转型为一家更偏向 AI 原生公司的关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, talk more about that.
zh: 好的，多谈谈那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean?
zh: 那是什么意思？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that look like?
zh: 那看起来像什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is that so important?
zh: 为什么这如此重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we were in our mature phase, so when Square was working quite well, it was a very large business, and then we had started Cash App and that also followed suit.
zh: 所以当我们处于成熟阶段时，当 Square 运作良好时，它是一笔非常大的生意，然后我们启动了 Cash App，那也紧随其后。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had spun them out almost as what we call a GM structure.
zh: 我们几乎把它们分离出来，也就是我们所谓的 GM 结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they were effectively run as a portfolio of independent companies and they had their own CEOs who all reported to Jack and it was still one single executive team, but they had separate engineering practices, they had separate design teams.
zh: 所以它们实际上作为一个独立公司的投资组合来运营，它们有自己的 CEO，都向 Jack 汇报，它仍然是一个单一的执行团队，但它们有独立的工程实践，它们有独立的设计团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were kind of separate in almost every way except for some shared resources like our foundational resources like legal and some platforms and things like that.
zh: 它们几乎在各方面都是分开的，除了像我们的基础资源（如法律）以及一些平台之类的一些共享资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that that was very useful for us for the stage of company that we were in, but when you really want to go deep in technology, when you really want to connect with these things that are industry changing events that are happening, you need a singular focus, and we changed the organization.
zh: 所以我认为这对我们来说，对于我们所在的那个公司阶段是非常有用的，但是当你真的想在技术上深入钻研，当你真的想与这些正在发生的行业变革性事件建立联系时，你需要一个单一的焦点，我们改变了组织架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all engineers report into one single team now, all designers report into one single team and there's single head of engineering, single head of design, et cetera.
zh: 所以现在所有的工程师都汇报给同一个单一的团队，所有的设计师都汇报给同一个单一的团队，只有一个工程负责人，一个设计负责人，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was the big transformation that we made, and that meant we could really drive forward AI, we could drive forward platform and just technical depth generally.
zh: 这是我们所做的重大变革，这意味着我们可以真正推动 AI 发展，我们可以真正推动平台发展，以及整体上的技术深度。

speaker: Unknown
en: For companies that are struggling with this potentially or trying to figure out how to do this, two things I'm hearing here is start to see yourself as a technology company.
zh: 对于那些可能正在为此挣扎或试图弄清楚如何去做的公司，我在这里听到的两件事是，开始将自己视为一家技术公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't necessarily apply to every company, but seems like an important element is like we're building technology, we're not a financial company, we're not a real estate company, we're not a technology company.
zh: 这不一定适用于每一家公司，但似乎一个重要的因素是，我们在构建技术，我们不是一家金融公司，我们不是一家房地产公司，我们不是一家技术公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then two is organize the team such that say engineers report up to an engineering leader versus a GM who maybe doesn't understand engineering as well or doesn't take it as seriously as they should.
zh: 然后第二点是组织团队，比如说工程师向工程负责人汇报，而不是向一个可能不那么懂工程或者没有把工程当回事的 GM 汇报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that's pretty much what we did.
zh: 是的，我认为我们基本上就是这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not to lean too heavily on this, but this is what jobs did when he came back to Apple as well.
zh: 虽然不想过度强调这一点，但这也就是乔布斯当年回到苹果时所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He reorganized Apple to be functional, and it wasn't like we were following a playbook.
zh: 他将苹果重组为职能型组织，这并不是说我们在遵循某种剧本。

speaker: Unknown
en: We discovered this as we were investigating what it's going to take to make these teams more tech-focused and to bring our DNA back to our roots, which really was putting engineering and design first, which is what technology first means to me.
zh: 我们是在调查这些团队究竟需要什么才能更加专注于技术，以及如何将我们的 DNA 带回到根源的过程中发现这一点的，这实际上就是把工程和设计放在首位，这就是“技术优先”对我的意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I would say to companies, find your DNA and really try to optimize for what that is in a very simple and clear way.
zh: 所以，是的，我想对公司们说，找到你们的 DNA，并尝试以一种非常简单和清晰的方式对其进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so you made a bunch of changes, you had this manifesto, everyone's on board, you made a bunch of changes.
zh: 好的，所以你们进行了一系列变革，你们有这个宣言，每个人都达成了一致，你们进行了一系列变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: Functional technology first, comparing the way that your say engineering team works today versus two or three years ago, what is most different?
zh: “技术优先”的职能化模式，对比一下比如说你们的工程团队现在的运作方式与两三年前相比，最大的不同是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone was on board, I'll tell you that.
zh: 并不是所有人都同意的，我可以告诉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was quite a painful transformation.
zh: 这是一个相当痛苦的转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that one of the things that I learned the most throughout this process is that Conway's Law can be really, really powerful.
zh: 我认为我在整个过程中学到的最重要的一件事之一是，康威定律真的非常非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's the law that basically says you ship your org structure.
zh: 这条定律基本上说你发布的软件就是你的组织架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what you're organized as in terms of teams, in terms of collaborating groups and your operating model matters a lot to what you build.
zh: 所以你们在团队方面、协作小组方面以及运营模式方面的组织方式，对你们构建的东西影响很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that that was essentially the biggest change is we had a lot of momentum in each of these silos, be it Cash App, be it Afterpay, be it Square or even TIDAL or music streaming service.
zh: 所以我认为这基本上是最大的变化，我们在这些孤岛中的每一个都有很大的惯性，无论是 Cash App，是 Afterpay，是 Square 甚至 TIDAL 或音乐流媒体服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And no one was really talking to each other, no one was really aligned on technical strategy on what we even wanted to be five years from now as a collective team.
zh: 没有人真正互相交谈，没有人在技术战略上真正达成一致，甚至对于我们作为一个团队想要在五年后成为什么样子也没有共识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all those things are different now.
zh: 所以现在所有这些事情都不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not saying it's perfect, there's still a long road ahead of us, but we at least speak the same language.
zh: 我并不是说它是完美的，我们要走的路还很长，但至少我们说同一种语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all have access to the same tools, we share the same policies.
zh: 我们都可以使用相同的工具，我们共享相同的政策。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a certain level of senior engineer means the same thing across the whole company.
zh: 所以一定级别的资深工程师在整个公司意味着同样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: People can move from one team to another's into an area of need.
zh: 人们可以从一个团队调到另一个团队去到一个需要的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these things are very different.
zh: 所有这些都是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to sum it up, I would say we're technically focused and we're focused on advancing technical excellence as a goal.
zh: 但总的来说，我会说我们要专注于技术，我们专注于推进技术卓越作为一个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that just really wasn't that true two to three years ago.
zh: 而这仅仅在两三年前还不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were other things we were optimizing for then.
zh: 那时候我们还在优化其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe going one level deeper in terms of how people actually work at a day.
zh: 也许更深入地看一下人们每天实际上是如何工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're looking at an engineering team, say the average engineering team and maybe also the top most optimal engineering team, how is the way they work today different from a couple of years ago?
zh: 所以如果你看一个工程团队，比如说一般的工程团队，也许还包括最优的工程团队，他们现在的工作方式与几年前相比有何不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the small, certain teams that are very, very AI natives or teams that are building AI first everywhere are working much differently than before because they're using vibe code tools and they're essentially building without writing lines of code by hand, and that just wasn't true through the three years ago.
zh: 在细节上，那些非常 AI 原生或在各处都优先构建 AI 的特定团队，与以前的工作方式大不相同，因为他们在使用 vibe coding 工具，他们基本上是在不手工写代码的情况下进行构建，而这在三年前是不存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it was true anywhere in the world.
zh: 我认为这在世界任何地方都不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's dramatically different in teams that are still working with very heavy legacy code bases.
zh: 所以这对于那些仍在处理非常繁重的遗留代码库的团队来说是截然不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's less true, but they're also encountering these background AI processes.
zh: 对于他们来说不那么明显，但他们也在遇到这些后台 AI 流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have these tools that run 24/7 or run in the CI pipeline and they're analyzing vulnerabilities.
zh: 所以我们有这些全天候 24/7 运行或在 CI 流水线中运行的工具，它们在分析漏洞。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're looking at even bugs filed on tickets and trying to build patches while engineers are asleep.
zh: 它们甚至在查看工单上提交的错误，并尝试在工程师睡觉时构建补丁。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they come in the next day and look at it.
zh: 所以他们第二天早上再来看它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would say there are a number of ways in which they're different, but different teams have adapted in different ways depending on how close they are to the tools.
zh: 所以我会说有很多方面是不同的，但不同的团队根据他们与工具的距离，以不同的方式进行了适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so let me lean into that AI piece, which is I think where you guys are most ahead of a lot of other companies.
zh: 好的，所以让我深入探讨一下 AI 这一部分，我认为这是你们领先于许多其他公司的最主要的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys built your own agent I think is how you describe Goose.
zh: 你们构建了自己的智能体，我想这就是你们描述 Goose 的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of talk about productivity gains through AI.
zh: 所以现在有很多关于通过 AI 提高生产力的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this camp of people are like, you don't understand how much productivity there is to gain from AI.
zh: 有这一派人说，你不了解通过 AI 可以获得多少生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the future, this is the way it's all going to work.
zh: 这是未来，这就是一切运作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all accelerating 10X.
zh: 我们都在加速 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also this camp where people are like, I'm so overhyped, nothing's working.
zh: 还有另一派人会说，我对这种炒作感到厌倦，什么都不奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: People talk about it.
zh: 人们都在谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these pilots are failing.
zh: 所有这些试点项目都失败了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody's actually adopting this at scale.
zh: 没有人真正在规模上采用这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like you're probably in that first camp.
zh: 我感觉你可能属于第一阵营。

speaker: Unknown
en: What sort of gains have you seen practically from AI tools on your teams?
zh: 你们在团队中从 AI 工具实际看到了什么样的收益？

speaker: Unknown
en: Our number one priority is through automate Block, which means getting AI and getting AI forms of automation through our entire company.
zh: 我们的首要任务是通过自动化 Block，这意味着让 AI 和 AI 形式的自动化贯穿我们的整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we feel that that's just at the beginning of where the utility is with all these large language models, and I think we're going to continue to see that improve.
zh: 我们认为这只是所有这些大语言模型实用性的开端，我认为我们将继续看到它的改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even now, we find engineering teams that are very, very AI forward that are using Goose every day are reporting about eight to 10 hours saved per week, and this is self-reported.
zh: 即使是现在，我们发现那些非常超前使用 AI、每天都在使用 Goose 的工程团队报告说每周节省了大约 8 到 10 小时，这是他们自己报告的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also have a number of check metrics to try and validate that.
zh: 然后我们还有许多检查指标来试图验证这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we look at PRs, we look at throughput of features, we look at a whole bunch of things and we have our data scientists come up with a complicated formula that tries to distill it all into something meaningful.
zh: 所以我们查看 PR（拉取请求），查看功能的吞吐量，查看一大堆事情，我们的数据科学家会想出一个复杂的公式试图将所有内容浓缩成有意义的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we feel across the whole company, we're probably trending towards 20 to 25% of manual hours saved.
zh: 我们感觉在整个公司范围内，我们可能正朝着节省 20% 到 25% 的人工工时的趋势发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's just the start of all of this.
zh: 我认为这仅仅是所有这一切的开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do feel that the more AI-native companies are doing a better job of realizing this.
zh: 我确实觉得那些更加 AI 原生的公司在实现这一点方面做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So companies that started just with AI startups mostly, but there is some truth to this notion that AI isn't a panacea and it's growing as well in capability.
zh: 所以那些主要从 AI 创业公司起步的公司，但 AI 并非灵丹妙药，而且其能力也在增长这种说法也有一些道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need to ride that wave along with it.
zh: 所以你需要随之一同驾驭这股浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of the companies aren't realizing this.
zh: 我认为许多公司没有意识到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, "Well, where's the value?"
zh: 他们会说，“好吧，价值在哪里？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And the truth is the value is changing every day.
zh: 真相是价值每天都在变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need to be adaptable and look at what the value is today and plan for what the value will be tomorrow and then slowly expand to the areas where it's most efficacious.
zh: 所以你需要适应性强，看看今天的价值是什么，并规划明天的价值，然后慢慢扩展到它最有效的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you an example.
zh: 我给你举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: One area in which we find that it's really good is for non-technical teams to be able to build little software tools for themselves.
zh: 我们发现它真正擅长的一个领域是让非技术团队能够为自己构建小型软件工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this has been one of the most surprising and energizing uses of Goose within Block is we'll have our enterprise risk management team build a whole system for self-servicing enterprise risk, and this is compressing weeks of work into hours, or ordinarily, they would be waiting for an internal apps team or something to go and build that and they would put that on their Q2 roadmap and everyone would be twiddling their thumbs until it all clicked into place, but now you can just go and do it.
zh: 所以这是 Goose 在 Block 内部最令人惊讶和振奋的用途之一，我们的企业风险管理团队构建了一个用于自助式企业风险的完整系统，这将几周的工作压缩到了几个小时，通常情况下，他们需要等待内部应用团队或其他团队去构建它，他们会把它放在第二季度的路线图上，所有人都会在那之前无所事事，直到一切就位，但现在你可以直接去做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of these kinds of use cases we're seeing an enormous amount of productivity gain in the other area, which I'm really excited about is we have this other tool called Gosling, which is a goose for mobile effectively.
zh: 所以我们看到许多这类用例在其他领域产生了巨大的生产力收益，另一个我真正感到兴奋的领域是我们有另一个叫 Gosling 的工具，它实际上是一个用于移动端的 Goose。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it operates your Android OS at a native level using the accessibility API.
zh: 所以它在原生层面使用无障碍 API 操作你的 Android 操作系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we use that for automating UI tests.
zh: 我们用它来自动化 UI 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So before, you would have to hire an army of contractors or QAs who would go and click through every screen, but now we can just bake those into automated tests and then give you a report at the end.
zh: 在此之前，你必须雇佣一支由承包商或 QA 组成的庞大队伍去点击每一个屏幕，但现在我们可以把它们直接嵌入到自动化测试中，然后在最后给你一份报告。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're seeing a lot of advantages in those types of areas, but where you have a lot of depth and a lot of really strong people come together is where AI, I think still underperforms humans.
zh: 所以我们在这些类型的领域看到了很多优势，但是当你拥有很多深度和很多非常强的人聚集在一起的地方，AI 表现仍然不如人类的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's something that's probably going to get better over time, but it's also something where we should lean into as humans.
zh: 这一点可能会随着时间的推移而变好，但这也是我们作为人类应该深入的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you have some very senior engineers and they're thinking about things like architecture and design and race conditions, orchestration, things like this, that's still an area where AI isn't quite there.
zh: 所以当你有一些非常资深的工程师，他们在思考架构和设计以及竞态条件、编排这类事情时，这仍然是 AI 尚未完全涉足的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the companies that aren't feeling the success in AI are trying to just throw these tools at their giant code bases and hoping good things will happen, and that's not how it's playing out.
zh: 我认为那些没有在 AI 中感受到成功的公司，试图只是将这些工具扔给他们庞大的代码库并希望发生好事，而这并不是正在发生的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eventually, I do think it'll get there, but right now we're still in the early utility phase.
zh: 最终，我确实认为它会达到那个地步，但现在我们仍处于早期的实用阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Holy moly, there's so much there in what you just shared.
zh: 天哪，你刚才分享的内容里有太多的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like five things I want to follow up on.
zh: 大约有五件事我想进一步追问。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so one is this metric you kind of alluded to, which is how you measure the impact of AI in your team.
zh: 好的，其中一件是你刚才提到的那个指标，也就是你如何衡量 AI 在你团队中的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was human manual hours saved, is that how you describe it?
zh: 所以它是人工工时节省，你是这样描述的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's correct.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's roughly a fourth of an engineer's time currently is being saved by AI tooling.
zh: 所以目前大约有四分之一的工程师时间被 AI 工具节省了下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: That metric is across all teams.
zh: 这个指标涵盖了所有团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that would be our support teams, our legal teams, our risk teams, all of them together.
zh: 所以这包括我们的支持团队、法务团队、风险团队，所有这些加在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on the engineering side, it's very variable because like I said before, it matters how big and how complex the code base is.
zh: 然后在工程方面，它是变化很大的，因为正如我之前所说，代码库有多大和多复杂很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're building a totally new Greenfields code base or you're building an app for a new platform, then we're seeing those pretty aggressive gains, but in very complex code bases that already exist, those gains are not quite there yet.
zh: 所以如果你正在构建一个全新的 Greenfields 代码库或者你正在为一个新平台构建一个应用，那么我们看到了那些相当激进的收益，但在已经存在的非常复杂的代码库中，那些收益还没有完全达到。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And whenever I hear a stat like this, I think an important element that people need to think about is this is the worst it will ever be.
zh: 每当我听到这样的统计数据时，我认为人们需要考虑的一个重要因素是，这是它有史以来最糟糕的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the lowest, this is now the baseline.
zh: 这是最低点，这是现在的基线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it may not sound that crazy yet, but it's going to get crazy.
zh: 所以它现在听起来可能没那么疯狂，但它会变得疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, the other thing that you talked about is Goose, you haven't explained what Goose is.
zh: 好的，你谈到的另一件事是 Goose，你还没有解释什么是 Goose。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a huge deal.
zh: 这是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Explain what Goose is and how important this has become to you guys.
zh: 解释一下什么是 Goose 以及它对你们来说变得多么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Goose is a general purpose AI agent.
zh: 所以 Goose 是一个通用的 AI 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can think of it as a desktop tool or a program that you can download and install on your computer and then it has a UI.
zh: 所以你可以把它看作是一个桌面工具或一个可以下载并安装在你电脑上的程序，然后它有一个 UI。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can talk to it just like a chatbot and you can say anything from, "Hey Goose, organize my photos by category, and it has the ability to look within your photos and if there are a lot of trees, it'll organize them as nature photos.
zh: 你可以像和聊天机器人一样和它交谈，你可以说的任何话从，“嘿 Goose，按类别整理我的照片”，它有能力查看你的照片，如果有很多树，它会将它们整理为自然照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are a lot of people, it'll organize them as portraiture."
zh: 如果有很多人，它会将它们整理为肖像摄影。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of this sort of stuff to writing software for you.
zh: 所有这些事情都为你编写软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it can do all of these tasks, and the way we've been able to do this is through something called a model context protocol or the MCP, which a lot of your listeners might've heard.
zh: 所以它可以做所有这些任务，而我们能够做到这一点的方式是通过一种称为模型上下文协议或 MCP 的东西，你的很多听众可能听说过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is something that Anthropic came up with that we were a very early contributor to.
zh: 这是 Anthropic 想出来的，而我们要非常早的贡献者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the model context protocol is very simply just a set of formalized wrappers around existing tools or existing capabilities.
zh: 模型上下文协议非常简单，就是围绕现有工具或现有能力的一套形式化封装。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you have tools that you use in the enterprise, be it Salesforce or be it Snowflake or SQL, any of these things, you can wrap them in the MCP and then it exposes them to your LLM to be able to manipulate.
zh: 所以如果你在企业中有使用的工具，比如 Salesforce 或 Snowflake 或 SQL，任何这些东西，你可以把它们封装在 MCP 中，然后它将这些暴露给你的 LLM 以便进行操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So until that point, the LLMs were not really able to do much other than chat, but Goose gives these brains arms and legs to go out and act in our digital world, and that's where we find it's had most impact and it's built on this fairly open protocol that anyone can implement.
zh: 所以在那之前，LLM 除了聊天之外真的不能做太多事情，但 Goose 给了这些大脑手臂和腿，走出去在我们的数字世界中行动，这就是我们发现它产生最大影响的地方，并且它是建立在这个任何人都可以实现的相当开放的协议之上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There have been an explosion of MCPs.
zh: MCP 已经出现了爆发式增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Goose is entirely open source, by the way, so any of you can download it and extend it, write your own MCPs, and that's been our core successes through Goose.

zh: 最终结果变成了，现在需要一年甚至更多的时间才能让它恢复到原来的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so interesting that AI now can make that possible, and what you're saying is that's actually maybe the way you should be working.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the trick is getting the AI to respect all of those incremental improvements, yeah, and sort of bake those in as a part of the specification, if you will.
zh: 我认为诀窍在于让 AI 尊重所有那些增量改进，是的，并如果你愿意的话，把它们作为规范的一部分融入进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the point you made about this agent, just you give it a bunch of ideas that builds them overnight and then you could see, I imagine it goes even further up the stack and comes up with the ideas and then starts building them and then you're like, "Okay, oh, that was a great idea.
zh: 另外，你刚才关于这个智能体说的这一点，只是你给它一堆想法，它在一夜之间构建它们，然后你就能看到，我想象它会进一步深入堆栈并想出想法，然后开始构建它们，然后你会像，“好的，噢，那是个很棒的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I can see it immediately in the same workflow."
zh: 现在我可以在同一个工作流中立即看到它。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's true.
zh: 是的，那是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was actually literally trying what you're saying just last week.
zh: 实际上上周我真的在尝试你所说的这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I have this new version of Goose that we're working on and I was asking it to come up with ideas to improve itself and implement it overnight.
zh: 所以我们正在开发这个新版本的 Goose，我让它想出改进自己的想法并在一夜之间实现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes-
zh: 有时候——

speaker: Unknown
en: Slip problem.
zh: 滑动问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: ... Sometimes it kind of goes off the script entirely and you have to sort of pull it back a bit.
zh: ……有时候它完全偏离了剧本，你必须把它稍微拉回来一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're not quite at that era where it's completely self-improving and completely autonomous, but I do think we're in a transition phase where we can give it that nudge and say, "Hey, here's my wishlist of 10 things that I wish you could do.
zh: 所以我认为我们还没完全处于那个它完全自我改进和完全自主的时代，但我确实认为我们正处于一个过渡阶段，我们可以给它那个推动力并说，“嘿，这是我希望你能做的 10 件事的愿望清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go and figure out the best way to do them."
zh: 去找出做它们的最佳方式。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's successful I would say on 60% of those things, if the features are well enough described and it struggles on the remaining 40 where you have to kind of intervene and massage it.
zh: 我会说如果这些功能被描述得足够好，它在 60% 的这些事情上是成功的，而在剩下的 40% 中它会挣扎，你必须稍微干预一下并给它按摩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh man, I'm just imagining this feature where you give it the goal of drive revenue and growth and then it's just like, "Okay, everyone's fired.
zh: 天哪，我只是在想象这个功能，你给它推动收入和增长的目标，然后它就像，“好的，所有人都被解雇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's your paychecks.
zh: 这是你们的支票。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll take it from here."
zh: 我会从这里接手。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we're going to be there.
zh: 我不认为我们会到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think we're going to need a lot of human taste to anchor these AIs so they don't go off script to be honest.
zh: 我确实认为我们需要很多人类的品味来锚定这些 AI，这样它们说实话就不会偏离剧本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really where our design lead and our design teams are pushing us to think, and that's a differentiator that I think will push us beyond this era of AI slop that everyone's talking about.
zh: 这真的是我们的设计主管和设计团队正在推动我们思考的地方，也是我认为将把我们推超出每个人都在谈论的 AI 垃圾时代的那个差异化因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, it's very much anchoring it into a thing that matters to people and the thing that's tasteful and useful and has value.
zh: 所以是的，非常多的是将其锚定到一个对人们重要的事情上，锚定到一个有品味、有用且有价值的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: To make that even more concrete, is there an example of something maybe AI was trying to, or a team was trying to pitch where you had to just know this is where humans are going to step in and keep things on track?
zh: 为了让这一点更加具体，是否有一个例子，也许是 AI 试图做的事情，或者一个团队试图推销的事情，你必须知道这就是人类要介入并保持事情正轨的地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say it was more around things like process automation or a lot of times I'll get this sort of request where a team will say, "We need to buy this new tool from this vendor because our current tool is entering X, Y and Z."
zh: 我说这更多是围绕流程自动化这类事情，或者很多时候我会收到这种请求，一个团队会说，“我们需要从这个供应商购买这个新工具，因为我们当前的工具正在进入 X、Y 和 Z。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Another team will say, "No, no, no, we can just use Goose to build an app that will do the same thing for us in half the time or less."
zh: 另一个团队会说，“不，不，不，我们可以直接使用 Goose 构建一个应用来为我们做同样的事情，时间减半或更少。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as a human, you're sitting there thinking, "Is any of this necessary?
zh: 然后作为一个人，你坐在那里思考，“这一切真的有必要吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: If we just change the process, do we even need to think about building tools?"
zh: 如果我们只是改变流程，我们甚至还需要考虑构建工具吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the thing that AI isn't good at, it's not able to have this portfolio judgment or judgment across a global sense of what's important and what matters.
zh: 这就是 AI 不擅长的事情，它无法拥有这种组合判断或基于对重要性和重要意义的全局感的判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of times, I tell teams just question the base assumption, particularly our InfoSec teams because they'll twist themselves into knot sometimes trying to secure something and you'll be like, "We'll just ask the team that's building it to do it differently or to not build that at all if it doesn't matter, and then you won't have to increase your surface area of securing it."
zh: 所以很多时候，我告诉团队要质疑基本假设，特别是我们的 InfoSec 团队，因为有时他们会把自己打结试图保护某些东西，你会像，“我们只是要求构建它的团队以不同的方式做这件事，或者如果它不重要就不要构建它，然后你就不必增加你保护它的表面积。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think those are the areas where it's better for a human to use judgment and AI has not done a great job.
zh: 所以我认为这些领域更适合人类使用判断力，而 AI 做得不是很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You make this point about building your own software, your own tools instead of buying stuff.
zh: 你提出了关于构建你自己的软件、你自己的工具而不是购买东西的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a big question with AI, is it's going to replace all these SaaS apps to Salesforce over.
zh: 这是 AI 的一个大问题，它是否会取代所有这些 SaaS 应用从而取代 Salesforce。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a sense of just either how much money you guys have maybe saved building your own stuff, or have you built a new-found respect for the existing SaaS software that everyone's using and pays lots of money for?
zh: 是否有一种感觉，要么是你们通过构建自己的东西省了多少钱，或者是你们对现有的每个人都在使用并为此支付大量资金的 SaaS 软件产生了新的尊重？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a trap in getting away from your core purpose as a company.
zh: 我认为这里有一个陷阱，就是偏离了作为公司的核心目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our core purpose is economic empowerment.
zh: 而我们的核心目标是经济赋权。

speaker: Unknown
en: So getting customers or merchants or artists the ability to make a sale or pay their rent or upload their latest creation to TIDAL.
zh: 所以让客户或商家或艺术家能够进行销售或支付房租或将他们最新的创作上传到 TIDAL。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that anything that serves that purpose, we should encourage and we should invest in, but if we're just purely looking at dollars versus dollars, then that's pulling us off that purpose.
zh: 我认为任何服务于那个目的的事情，我们都应该鼓励并投资，但如果我们纯粹只是看美元对美元，那正在把我们拉离那个目的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The savings and costs that there might be in replacing a vendor tool by something you build in-house is probably not worth it in the mental bandwidth that you've lost and the amount of the team's technical focus that's being taken away.
zh: 通过用内部构建的东西取代供应商工具可能带来的节省和成本，可能是不值得的，考虑到你失去的精神带宽和被占用团队技术专注力的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I would say it just keep coming to the thing that matters to you as a company and then the rest will follow from that.
zh: 所以是的，我会说它总是回归到对你作为一家公司重要的事情上，然后其余的会随之而来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think people forget just how much maintenance it takes to keep something you've built.
zh: 是的，我认为人们忘记了维护你自己构建的东西需要多少维护。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, "Okay, cool, we built it in a weekend and now it's years of endless maintenance and requests and support."
zh: 就像，“好的，很酷，我们在一个周末构建了它，现在是多年的无尽维护、请求和支持。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And also to your point, it feels like it comes back to the always motto of just focus on your core competencies and then buy everything else.
zh: 而且还要回到你的观点，感觉它回到了那个永恒的座右铭，只关注你的核心竞争力，然后购买其他一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's the classic 80/20 problem, and we have that enough with the apps that we build for our customers.
zh: 是的，这就是经典的 80/20 问题，在我们为客户构建的应用中，我们已经受够了这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll build some great experiments that really resonate, and then we have to spend a lot of time ironing out the long tail of problems.
zh: 我们会构建一些真正引起共鸣的出色实验，然后我们必须花费大量时间去解决长尾问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in Cash Card, for example, we built the entire functionality of Cash Card, I would say pretty much in a weekend or maybe a week of integration and work.
zh: 例如在 Cash Card 中，我们构建了 Cash Card 的全部功能，我可以说基本上是在一个周末，或者一周的集成和工作时间内完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it took a really long time to iron out all these edge cases where someone would tip twice the value of the bill and then it would completely break something in the back end, or people would use it as a gas station and they have a different way of billing your card.
zh: 然后花了很长时间来解决所有这些边缘情况，比如有人会付双倍账单金额的小费，然后这会完全破坏后端的某些东西，或者人们在加油站使用它，而它们有不同的计费方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, it's very much that.
zh: 所以是的，非常像那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to your point, I would always come back to what is the reason we're doing this?
zh: 关于你的观点，我总是会回到我们做这件事的原因上？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why does it matter to us and to our customers?
zh: 为什么它对我们和我们的客户很重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it doesn't clearly satisfy that, I would just push it off as a not interesting thing.
zh: 如果它不能清楚地满足这一点，我就把它推到一边，认为它不是一件有趣的事情。

en: One of the biggest parts of the conversation around AI is hiring jobs, things like that.
zh: 围绕 AI 的对话中最大的部分之一是招聘、工作之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have two kind of this two-part question.
zh: 所以我有两个这个两步式的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is just how has the rise of all these AI tools, this increased productivity impacted the way you plan head counts and hire?
zh: 一个是，所有这些 AI 工具的兴起，这种提高的生产力，是如何影响你规划人员编制和招聘的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what do you look for that's different in people you're hiring now that AI is such a big part of the way you guys work?
zh: 那么，鉴于 AI 已经成为你们工作方式的重要组成部分，你在现在招聘的人身上寻找哪些不同的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that things have progressed far enough that it's really impacted in a fundamental way how many people you would need to build an app of the scale of Cash App, for example.
zh: 我认为事情还没有发展到足以从根本上改变构建像 Cash App 这样规模的应用程序需要多少人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's changed for us is much different and it has nothing to do with AI, it's what we talked about earlier is moving from our GM structure to a functional structure.
zh: 我认为对我们来说改变的东西是非常不同的，它与 AI 无关，就是我们之前谈到的从 GM 结构转向职能结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in our GM structure, our incentives were always to think of engineering headcount as a commodity.
zh: 在我们的 GM 结构中，我们的激励总是将工程人数视为一种商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we would just add more engineers if we wanted to build more features and the classic mythical man person month trap or whatever it's called.
zh: 所以如果我们想构建更多功能，我们就会增加更多工程师，这就陷入了经典的人月神话陷阱，或者不管它叫什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that moving to a functional structure completely changes that and you're like, "Well, we can leverage common platforms, common modules, we can bring in experts from across the company to advise us on how better to do this."
zh: 我认为转向职能结构完全改变了这一点，你会想，“嗯，我们可以利用通用平台、通用模块，我们可以引入全公司的专家来建议我们如何更好地做到这一点。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those kinds of things I think have made it much different and how we hire and we no longer see engineers as a commodity to just add 100 people to go and build the next product in Cash App.
zh: 所以我认为这些事情使我们的招聘方式发生了很大变化，我们不再把工程师看作是一种商品，仅仅为了构建 Cash App 中的下一个产品而增加 100 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on the AI side, we're very much looking for people that are embracing these tools and that are eager to try and learn from it.
zh: 但在 AI 方面，我们非常渴望寻找那些拥抱这些工具并渴望尝试和从中学习的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not looking for people who are amazing AI practitioners on the get-go.
zh: 我们不是在寻找那些一开始就是令人惊叹的 AI 从业者的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we have those people and we're interested in those people if they ever want to work with us.
zh: 我认为我们有这样的人，如果他们想为我们工作，我们对此感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm much more keen on looking for that college grad who just really is eager to learn about these tools and open to it, or even the veteran who has embraced these tools and figured it out.
zh: 但我更热衷于寻找那种刚刚真正渴望了解这些工具并对其持开放态度的大学毕业生，或者是那些已经拥抱这些工具并搞懂了它们的老手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of where we're optimizing for who we look for rather than a specific set of skills.
zh: 这就是我们要优化寻找谁的地方，而不是寻找一套特定的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So essentially the biggest change is just looking for people that are embracing AI, not being like, "No, I don't need this stuff.
zh: 所以本质上最大的变化只是寻找那些拥抱 AI 的人，而不是像这样，“不，我不需要这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm an amazing engineer.
zh: 我是一名令人惊叹的工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need to use Cursor or Goose or all these things."
zh: 我不需要使用 Cursor 或 Goose 或所有这些东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, a learning mindset is how I would put it.
zh: 是的，我会把这称之为一种学习心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something that Jack our CEO talks about a lot is he wants us to be a learning first company.
zh: 这是我们的 CEO Jack 经常谈论的事情，他希望我们成为一家学习优先的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everything we do, every experiment that we ship, what can we learn from it and did we feel that we gave it our best shot?
zh: 所以我们所做的一切，我们发布的每一个实验，我们能从中学到什么，我们觉得我们尽力了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that that's more important to him than even sort of coming up with the right business answer every time.
zh: 我认为对他来说，这比每次都提出正确的商业答案更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about when you're interviewing?
zh: 那当你在面试的时候呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you encouraging engineers to use AI tools as they're doing exercises?
zh: 你在鼓励工程师在做练习时使用 AI 工具吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How did that change over the past year or two?
zh: 这在过去一两年里是如何变化的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we're starting to do that now.
zh: 是的，我们现在开始这样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So traditionally we would just use CoderPad or something like that to wipe boards or a problem or even program it in Pseudocode or near Pseudocode.
zh: 传统上我们只会使用 CoderPad 或类似的东西来擦板或一个题目，甚至用伪代码或接近伪代码来编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now we're looking at can you use Vibe code to build something?
zh: 但现在我们在看你能否使用 Vibe code 来构建东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: How comfortable are you with these tools or how are you thinking about evolving with them as well?
zh: 你对这些工具有多适应，或者你也在考虑如何随着它们进化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's early days yet I would say that it's not clear to me that necessarily how someone knows how to use, be it Goose or Cursor or any of these other tools matters that much to whether they're a good engineer.
zh: 但我还认为这尚属早期阶段，对我来说还不清楚，一个人如何知道如何使用 Goose 或 Cursor 或任何其他这些工具，与他们是否是一名好的工程师有多大关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I still think that things that we interviewed for in the past, a critical mindset, the ability to really understand deeply the technical nature of a problem is still much more important than whether you're a fully AI native programmer or not.
zh: 我仍然认为我们过去在面试中寻找的东西，批判性思维，真正深入理解问题技术本质的能力，仍然比你是否是一个完全 AI 原生的程序员重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another question that I've always been thinking about a lot of people wonder is what level of engineer is most benefiting from these tools?
zh: 我一直在思考的另一个问题，也是很多人想知道的，是什么级别的工程师最受益于这些工具？

speaker: Unknown
en: You could argue it's the junior engineers now, they could just get all this work done.
zh: 你可以认为是初级工程师，现在他们可以把所有这些工作做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could argue it's senior engineers because they know so much more about how things work and now they could just orchestrate thousands of agents doing their bidding.
zh: 你可以认为是高级工程师，因为他们对工作原理了解得更多，现在他们可以指挥数千个智能体为他们工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you seen in terms of which level is benefiting most?
zh: 就哪个层级获益最多这一点，你看到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so two answers to that.

en: Looking back at your time at Block, I keep trying to, I almost say Square because I'm so used to that over the air, but I know Block is the name of the broader company and Square is just one.
zh: 回顾你在 Block 的时光，我一直试着，我差点说了 Square，因为我太习惯那个称呼了，但我知道 Block 是更广泛的公司名称，而 Square 只是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just so people understand, Square is one business unit, one product within Block.
zh: 只是为了让大家理解，Square 是 Block 下的一个业务单元，一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Correct, yeah, we have Square, Afterpay, Cash App and TIDAL are four major brands, and then we also have Bitkey and Proto that are focused on Bitcoin for us and we chip hardware in those two brands.
zh: 对的，是的，我们有 Square、Afterpay、Cash App 和 TIDAL 四个主要品牌，然后我们还有 Bitkey 和 Proto，专注于我们的比特币业务，我们在这两个品牌中生产硬件芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, great.
zh: 好的，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that some people are like, what are you guys talking about?
zh: 我想有些人会像，你们在谈论什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, cool.
zh: 好的，酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So reflecting back on your time at Block, what's maybe the most counterintuitive lesson you've learned about building products or building teams that goes against what most people believe, say common startup wisdom?
zh: 那么回顾你在 Block 的时光，关于构建产品或构建团队，你所学到的最反直觉的经验是什么？它是与大多数人的信念相反的，比如说常见的初创公司智慧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think code quality is one.
zh: 我认为代码质量算一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being an engineer.
zh: 做一名工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned this very early on and it keeps coming true over and over and over again.
zh: 我很早就学到了这一点，而且它一次又一次地不断被验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of engineers think that code quality is important to building a successful product.
zh: 许多工程师认为代码质量对于构建成功的产品很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The two have nothing to do with each other, but my favorite example is YouTube.
zh: 这两者毫无关系，但我最喜欢的例子是 YouTube。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was working at Google around the time YouTube was acquired and I just remember there was this whole wash of angst about how horrible the YouTube code base is and how terrible their architecture is, and they're storing videos as blobs in MySQL and whatnot.
zh: 我在 Google 工作的时候大约是 YouTube 被收购的时候，我只记得有一大波焦虑，关于 YouTube 代码库有多么糟糕，他们的架构有多么糟糕，他们把视频作为 blob 存储在 MySQL 中等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could argue that YouTube is the most successful product at Google by a long way, maybe more successful than many of their others combined.
zh: 你可以争辩说 YouTube 是 Google 最成功的产品，遥遥领先，也许比其他许多产品的总和还要成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it really has very little to do with how well it was architected because the flip side of that Google video, which is product that I don't know if people remember, it existed before YouTube.
zh: 所以它真的与架构的优劣关系不大，因为另一方面是 Google Video，那个产品我不知道人们是否记得，它在 YouTube 之前就存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It supported more formats, it supported higher resolution.
zh: 它支持更多格式，它支持更高分辨率。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could upload hour long videos, YouTube had none of this.
zh: 你可以上传长达一小时的视频，YouTube 当时完全没有这些功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just had the one or two minute quick video thing and it's far and away, blown away its competition.
zh: 它只有一两分钟的快速视频功能，而且它远远地，彻底击败了竞争对手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think just keeping that front and center is why are we building these tools or these apps or these products?
zh: 所以我认为只是把这一点放在首位：我们为什么要构建这些工具或应用程序或产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: They're for people to solve a specific problem.
zh: 它们是为了让人们解决特定的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in our case, it's for a square merchant to make a sale, to sell coffee to you or to sell something they've made.
zh: 所以在我们的例子中，它是为了让 Square 商户达成销售，向你卖咖啡或出售他们制作的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really what's important.
zh: 这才是真正重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not really important how well our Android platform performs unless it's serving that need.
zh: 我们的 Android 平台的性能表现如何并不重要，除非它服务于那个需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's been a really hard one for me over my career.
zh: 所以我认为这在我的职业生涯中对我来说真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I continually encounter engineers who think we need to refactor, we need to do this in a better way.
zh: 我不断遇到认为我们需要重构的工程师，我们需要以更好的方式来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'm like, "No, all this code could be thrown away tomorrow.
zh: 然后我会说，“不，所有这些代码明天都可能被扔掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just focus on what we're trying to build and whom we're trying to build for."
zh: 所以只关注我们要构建什么以及我们要为谁构建。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That is an incredible insight and lesson.
zh: 这是一个令人难以置信的见解和教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: This YouTube story is so fun and such a good example.
zh: 这个 YouTube 的故事太有趣了，是一个非常好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're saying they were storing the video content in a MySQL set like row and column as a blob data.
zh: 你是说他们把视频内容存储在 MySQL 集合中，就像行和列作为 blob 数据一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, this is what, I didn't actually look the code so I couldn't verify it, but this was the common wisdom.
zh: 是的，这就是，我实际上没有看过代码所以我无法验证它，但这是当时的普遍认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they had an entirely Python stack that was incredibly slow compared to the state-of-the-art C++ and Java servers that we had hyper-optimized at Google back in those days.
zh: 然后他们有一个完整的 Python 栈，与我们当时在 Google 超优化的最先进的 C++ 和 Java 服务器相比，速度极慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is hilarious.
zh: 太搞笑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes me think about also companies when you look inside a company, if you work at a company, you're just like, "This is just pure chaos.
zh: 这也让我想到了公司，当你观察一家公司内部时，如果你在一家公司工作，你会想，“这纯粹就是混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one knows what's going on.
zh: 没有人知道发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is just about to all fall apart."
zh: 这一切即将分崩离析。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's basically what it's like at every successful hyper-growth company.
zh: 而这基本上就是每家成功的超高速增长公司的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there's some truth to that for sure.
zh: 是的，这其中肯定有一些道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think again, it's just there's so much more that is more important to the success of a business.
zh: 所以我认为再次强调，对于企业的成功来说，还有更多更重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's what you said is are you solving a real problem for people?
zh: 就像你说的，你在为人们解决一个真正的问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you get in their hands?
zh: 你能把产品交到他们手中吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you continue solving real problems for them?
zh: 你能继续为他们解决实际问题吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not about the quality of the code, it's not how well you operate internally.
zh: 这不在于代码质量，也不在于你内部运作得有多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think on Cash App we had that as well.
zh: 我想我们在 Cash App 也有过那种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the early days of Cash App, I was head of engineering from when we were about 10 engineers to 200 plus and took us to about 10 plus or 20 million users thereabouts.
zh: 所以在 Cash App 的早期，我是工程主管，当时我们从大约 10 名工程师发展到了 200 多名，用户达到了一两千万左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was a very similar thing there.
zh: 那里有非常相似的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the outside it looked like everything was really chaotic.
zh: 从外面看，一切似乎真的很混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like people would build random experiments and ship them and it just didn't look like we were following strict policies on things like software life cycle and stuff like that, and it was kind of true.
zh: 就像是人们会构建随意的实验，把它们发布出去，看起来我们没有在软件生命周期之类的事情上遵循严格的政策，这也有点真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my philosophy was always, we have all these brilliant engineers and I'm going to do more harm than good by trying to harness them into very strict blinkered areas.
zh: 我的哲学一直是，我们有这么多优秀的工程师，如果试图把他们限制在非常狭隘的领域，我会弊大于利。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they want to spin their wheels building something that is a complete waste of time for a little bit.
zh: 如果他们想白费力气去构建某种完全是浪费时间的东西，哪怕只有一小会儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, if they're delivering these amazing things on the flip side, then I'll almost allow that.
zh: 但同时，如果他们在另一方面交付了这些惊人的东西，那我几乎会允许那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll be okay with that.
zh: 我会对此表示同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a fine balance because engineers can really go off and into rabbit holes if you let them.
zh: 这是一个微妙的平衡，因为如果你让工程师放手去干，他们真的会误入歧途，钻进牛角尖。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, there's a certain amount of creativity that chaos breeds and you have to know how to build controlled chaos in some ways.
zh: 但是的，混乱会孕育一定程度的创造力，你必须懂得如何在某种程度上构建受控的混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have to create a foundation that isn't liable to rupture.
zh: 所以你必须创建一个不易破裂的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have major liability problems or something like that, or you're going to lose money in our case.
zh: 你会有重大责任问题之类的事情，或者在我们的情况下会赔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as long as those things are bedded down and you allow your engineers to have the freedom to experiment and iterate and do the things that energizes them, that's the ideal.
zh: 所以，只要这些基础夯实了，并且你允许你的工程师拥有实验和迭代的自由，做那些让他们充满活力的事情，那就是理想状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of controlled chaos, one of your titles during your time at Block, I guess this was while you were actually at Square, was Mad Scientist for four and a half years.
zh: 说到受控的混乱，你在 Block 期间的一个头衔，我想那实际上是你还在 Square 的时候，是疯狂科学家，当了四年半。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that was a time when I was working part-time, mostly because I had very young kids with lots of additional needs and I was a consultant on various different projects and I was trying to help some wacky things get off the ground.
zh: 是的，那是我兼职工作的一段时间，主要是因为我有非常年幼的孩子，有很多额外的需求，我是各种不同项目的顾问，我试图帮助一些古怪的事情起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, I'm really grateful to Block that they afforded me the freedom to have that role in my career as well.
zh: 是的，我真的很感激 Block 给了我这种自由，让我在职业生涯中也能拥有那个角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe one more question before I take us to Fail Corner, which I'll explain.
zh: 也许在我带大家进入“失败角”之前再问一个问题，我会解释一下的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've shared a few lessons of things you've learned over the course of your career.
zh: 所以你分享了一些你在职业生涯中学到的经验教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any other, just let's say core leadership lessons that you've learned that you think have been important to you being successful at the work that you've done?
zh: 还有其他的，就说核心领导力经验吧，你认为这些对你成功地完成工作很重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think start small with everything.
zh: 我认为万事都要从小处着手。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you try to boil the ocean to make a cup of tea, I don't know who said that, but it's a really a useful phrase that I keep coming back to.
zh: 如果你想煮沸整个海洋来泡一杯茶，我不知道是谁说的，但这真的是一个我一直回想起来的非常有用的短语。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll never get there.
zh: 你永远无法做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're making a cup of tea, just make the cup of tea.
zh: 所以如果你要泡茶，就只管泡那杯茶。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to boil all the water that there is.
zh: 你不需要把所有的水都煮沸。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sounds like really not delicious tea.
zh: 那听起来真的不是好喝的茶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ocean water.
zh: 海水。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's another one of, I think Carl Sagan said, "If you want to make an apple pie from scratch, you have to first invent the universe."
zh: 是的，我想还有另一个，我想是卡尔·萨根说的，“如果你想从头开始做一个苹果派，你必须先发明宇宙。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like narrow your scope to the thing that's in front of you and that's achievable.
zh: 所以就像是把你的范围缩小到你面前且可实现的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that I think is really important and that's one of our core tenets and always has been even when we were just Square in the early days, start small.
zh: 所以我认为这真的很重要，这也是我们的核心宗旨之一，而且一直以来都是，即使在我们早期只是 Square 的时候，也要从小处着手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there an example that maybe worked really well or maybe didn't work?
zh: 有没有什么例子效果特别好或者可能不太好？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, Goose started small.
zh: 有的，Goose 就是从小处着手的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just an engineer working on their own time trying to build something that was useful and that satisfied a thesis that they had.
zh: 它只是一名工程师在利用自己的时间尝试构建有用的东西，满足他们提出的一个论点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Brad, our creator of Goose, believed very early on, I think long before we heard the buzzword going around that agents would be how we unlock value from LLMs.
zh: 所以 Brad，我们的 Goose 的创造者，很早就相信，我想早在我们听到智能体这个流行词之前，他就相信智能体将是我们从 LLM 中释放价值的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he built a proof concept and he shared it with a bunch of people.
zh: 他构建了一个概念验证，并分享给了很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He shared it with Databricks and Anthropic, got them excited and learned a lot from them.
zh: 他把它分享给了 Databricks 和 Anthropic，让他们兴奋起来，并从他们那里学到了很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it just sort of built momentum from there.
zh: 所以它只是从那里建立起了势头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even internally, it was quite a similar thing.
zh: 甚至在内部，也是相当类似的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cash App itself was like that and Cash App started more or less as a hack week sort of idea and grew into a bigger and bigger and bigger thing.
zh: Cash App 本身就是那样的，Cash App 最初多多少少是一个黑客周的想法，然后成长得越来越大，越来越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of our projects start with these small experiments that we try to then build on top of.
zh: 所以我们的很多项目都是从这些小实验开始的，我们试图在此基础上进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: We became the very first company that was a public company to launch a Bitcoin product.
zh: 我们成为了第一家推出比特币产品的上市公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was again a hack week idea that actually Jack and me and another engineer worked on.
zh: 这又是一个黑客周的想法，实际上是我、Jack 和另一名工程师一起做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the hackathon team?
zh: 那是黑客马拉松团队吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You and Jack Dorsey and an engineer?
zh: 你和 Jack Dorsey 还有一名工程师？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was the three of us.
zh: 是的，就我们三个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unreal.
zh: 难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and it was great.
zh: 是的，而且那很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went and bought a cup of coffee, a blue bottle, and it was bought using Bitcoin over cash card.
zh: 我们去买了杯咖啡，一瓶蓝瓶咖啡，是用比特币通过现金卡买的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll tell you those in hindsight, probably the most expensive cup of coffee.
zh: 我要告诉你，事后看来，那可能是最贵的一杯咖啡。

speaker: Lenny
en: What was Bitcoin at? 20,000?
zh: 当时比特币是多少？2 万？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was 6,000 or 7,000 back then.
zh: 我觉得那时候是 6 千或 7 千。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like 120,000 now.
zh: 现在大概是 12 万了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 真棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, it's an example of how you get to a working useful product to people if you focus on a small thing first in a build.
zh: 是的，但这是一个例子，说明如果你先专注于构建中的一个小事物，你就能为人们提供一个可用的有用产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just to double down on this counter too.
zh: 我也想在这个反例上加倍下注。

speaker: Unknown
en: "Okay, we have a big idea, we're just going to put a bunch of resources on it and go big immediately."
zh: “好吧，我们有个大主意，我们要投入一堆资源，立即大干一场。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've been part of teams like that too.
zh: 我也曾是这类团队的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in my career, I worked at Google on this product called Google Wave, which was trying to be everything to everyone and we were 70, 80 engineers building this thing before it even really had any users outside Google.
zh: 所以在我的职业生涯中，我在谷歌从事过一款叫做 Google Wave 的产品，它试图成为所有人的所有东西，我们在 Google 之外甚至还没有任何用户之前，就有 70、80 个工程师在构建这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's an example of something that started big, tried to go big on day one and probably lacked some of that meeting the earth where reality lies and adapting accordingly.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个起步就很大、试图在第一天就大干一场，并且可能缺乏那种与现实接轨并据此适应的能力的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember Google Wave.
zh: 我记得 Google Wave。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was beautiful.
zh: 它很美。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of hype.
zh: 有很多炒作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't remember what it was for specifically, but it looked really nice.
zh: 我不记得具体是做什么用的，但它看起来真的很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, a lot of learnings from that one for me.
zh: 是的，我从那个项目中学到了很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What else?
zh: 还有什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Any other big lessons?
zh: 还有什么其他重要的教训吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Those two are the big ones, but I would also say question base assumptions on everything.
zh: 这两个是最大的教训，但我还要说，要对一切质疑基本假设。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes we get into traps where we are as professionals, hyper focused on what we're building that day, that week, that month.
zh: 有时候我们会陷入陷阱，作为专业人士，我们要么过度专注于那天、那周、那月在构建的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't stop to think should we even build this at all?
zh: 我们没有停下来思考我们到底应不应该构建这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or what's the purpose of building this?
zh: 或者构建这个的目的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Could we build something completely different that would matter more to our core reason for being?
zh: 我们能不能构建完全不同的东西，这对我们的核心存在理由更重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would say, yeah, question the sort of base assumptions.
zh: 所以我会说，是的，质疑这类基本假设。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's somewhat of a cliche, but you really need to remind yourself to apply it over and over and over again.
zh: 这有点陈词滥调，但你真的需要提醒自己一遍又一遍地应用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a colleague of yours on the podcast back in the day, IO, who worked with you on Cash App.
zh: 我以前在播客上请过你的一位同事，IO，他和你在 Cash App 上共事过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's a friend of mine, he's amazing.
zh: 他是我的朋友，他很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had a quote along those lines of just like, I forget exactly what it was, but it was just get to the bare metal of the thing that you're working on, just touch the thing that you're building and go to the base of it to really understand what's going on.
